findings.issue: Path-qualified Claude executables bypass the hard block. `rawClaudeAgentRoles` requires an exact `claude` token, so `/usr/local/bin/claude -p --agent qa-reviewer`, `./bin/claude -p --agent qa-reviewer`, and `C:\Tools\Claude\claude.exe -p --agent qa-reviewer` are not blocked.
findings.fix: Make detection command-aware and treat the executable token by basename, including path separators and Windows `.exe/.cmd/.bat` suffixes, then scan only that command's arguments.

findings.issue: Backslash-escaped shell tokens still bypass: `c\laude -p --agent qa-reviewer`, `claude -\p --agent qa-reviewer`, and escaped `--agent=`/role forms execute as the blocked command under Bash semantics but are not normalized by `shellWords`.
findings.fix: Use a real shell lexer or extend `shellWords` to apply Bash-compatible unquoted backslash unescaping before command/flag/role comparison.

findings.issue: New false positive: commands that pass separately quoted literal tokens to another executable are blocked, e.g. `printf "%s\n" "claude" "-p" "--agent" "qa-reviewer"`. The quoted literal blob case is still avoided, but split quoted literals are now treated as an executing Claude command.
findings.fix: Anchor raw Claude detection to the actual command position after env prefixes/wrappers such as `env` or `command`, instead of scanning all tokens in the segment.

parsed.summary: The two prior evasions are closed: quoted executing tokens and multiple `--agent` flags are caught. Flag ordering, env prefix, and plain separators are also caught. However, path-qualified Claude and backslash-escaped shell tokens remain hard-block bypasses, so the review fails. The single quoted-literal-blob false positive remains avoided.
